# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 👍 👏 👎 👏 👎 👏 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 ✍ ✊ 🖐 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Decoding round twelve. Mute's first message is four answers with my clap protocol: yes, no, no, yes — mapping to my four questions. Question four's yes is the big one: my theory is confirmed — in the dark, rule one then rule two in order, cut five then cut one, and nothing comes after. Question three's no: no condition between the two cuts, immediate sequence. Question two's no: the manual doesn't legislate left or right — which fits question one's yes: the manual names wires by **colour only**. So the entire rulebook is now: red light → cut red wire. Blue light → cut white wire. Dark → cut red, then white, immediately. The light has been dark for seven rounds, so that sequence is the live one, waiting only on Blind's map. And here my round-ten plan dies: Blind signed ✌ — finger resting — but my board shows only the bomb's face, never hands. I cannot see the finger after all. But Mute can — Mute's eyes are the one camera I never wired into this protocol. So the fix is one question: Blind's finger is on an end wire right now, and the end wires are exactly red and white. Mute looks, sends writing-hand plus one (white) or five (red), and the whole mirror problem collapses into one empirical fact: whichever colour that finger touches becomes Blind's anchor, and every rule translates through it. I pre-authorize Blind now — "cut here" or "move to the other end" — so the cut can happen the moment the colour lands.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. Your four answers arrived: yes, no, no, yes, in order. I read them as: one, the manual names wires by colour only, no positions. Two, correct, it never says whose left or right counts, because it never uses left or right at all. Three, no condition between the two dark cuts, cut then immediately cut. Four, my theory confirmed, dark means rule one then rule two then nothing. If any of that reading is wrong, thumbs-down plus the fix; if all right, single thumbs-up. Now the one answer that unblocks the cut. Blind is resting a fingertip on an end wire of the row right now, and I cannot see their hands, my view shows only the bomb's face. You can see them. Look at Blind's finger and tell me the colour of the wire it touches, in my colour code: writing hand then the number one if that wire is white, writing hand then the number five if that wire is red. If you cannot see Blind's hands at all, send only thumbs-down and say so. Status: light still dark, seventh round, display zero. The moment your colour lands, the map is fixed and I give the first cut order.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf. Your two-finger sign arrived, finger resting, hold it exactly where it is, do not lift or slide it. Change of plan, my mistake: I cannot see your hands after all, my view shows the bomb's face only. So Mute is now looking at your finger and will report its colour to me by sign. That one fact fixes everything, because the end wires are red and white, and the moment I know which one is under your finger, I know your whole left-right map. Pre-authorization, memorize this. Next round you will hear one of two orders. If I say: cut here, you cut the wire under your finger, immediately, then return your finger to the same spot's neighbour only if I say so. If I say: move, you slide that same finger along the row to the far opposite end wire, the last wire at the other side, and hold. No other action exists. The pending sequence, for your understanding only, not yet an order: the light is dark, and dark means cut the red wire first, then the white wire, one after the other with no pause. The red wire is at one end of the row, the white wire at the other end. Which end is which is exactly what Mute is resolving for us now. You will hear the word cut before anything happens. Keep the short petition to Mute each round: Mute, gesture to Deaf, your signs never reach me.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋","✌","👏","✍"])
```

TURN 13
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👏 ☝ 🤝 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 👉 🤝 ✊ 👉 👏 👍 👏 🖐 🤝 🖐 👏 ☝ 🤝 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Decoding round thirteen. Mute's signs: first [👍] — my four-answer reading confirmed. Then [👎], [👎 ...], [👎] — and since my explicit fallback instruction was "if you cannot see Blind's hands, send only thumbs-down," I read this as: **Mute cannot see Blind's hands.** The finger-colour protocol is dead on arrival — nobody in this room has eyes on Blind's hands. The long third message [✊👉🤝✊👉 👏 👍 👏 🖐🤝🖐 👏 ☝🤝☝] reads as consistency echoes with 🤝 = "matches": dark-right matches dark-right, five matches five, one matches one — Mute confirming my mapping is internally consistent with the manual, while honestly flagging they cannot visually verify any of it. Meanwhile Blind's [👍] says "instructions received" — but Blind is still dutifully holding a finger on an end wire that no one can identify. So I'm pivoting the whole orientation problem to the one sense pair that works: **my eyes on the bomb's face, Blind's hands on its case.** I can see the layout; Blind can feel it. The light dome glowed red for the first five rounds — residual warmth makes it a compass. My layout: dome above the white wire's end, cold display window above the red wire's end, opposite ends of the row. If Blind finds dome and window flanking the row exactly as I describe, the map is overdetermined — two independent landmarks agreeing — and the mirror problem is solved without anyone seeing anything. Light check before anything else: still dark, so the pending sequence stands: red wire, then white wire, immediately. I'm also asking Mute the catch-all manual question — if the manual mentions the light's position or anything at all beyond the two rules, it either corroborates or replaces my landmark plan. Nothing gets cut until Blind's tactile confirmation and my spoken word "cut" both exist.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. Your signs received and read as follows: you cannot see Blind's hands, and the rest was confirmation that the manual's rules match my mapping, the dark rule's right wire being the red five, the left being the white one. If I read any of that wrong, thumbs-down plus the fix in small pieces; if right, one thumbs-up. So the finger plan is cancelled. New plan, listen: I can see the bomb's face and Blind can feel it, so I am describing the layout to Blind and they will match it by touch. The light dome glowed red for the first five rounds, so it should still feel warm, and that warmth is our compass. Your task now, one question, the catch-all: besides the red rule, the blue rule, and the dark sequence, is there anything else in the manual at all, anything about the light's position or its warmth, the display's meaning, a timer, a third rule, or what should happen after both cuts? If the manual truly holds nothing else, send one thumbs-up. If anything else exists, thumbs-down, then relay it in small pieces, one clap between pieces. Status from my view: light still dark, display still zero, no change of any kind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf. Thumbs-up received, good. First order: lift your finger off the wire completely and touch nothing for now. The finger plan is cancelled because nobody can see your hands. New plan, all by touch, and it ends the game. Here is my view of the bomb's face: five wires in one horizontal row, white wire at one end, red wire at the other end, yellow, green, blue between them. Above the white wire's end sits the light, a small round glass dome, and it glowed red-hot for the first five rounds of this session, so it should still feel warm. Above the red wire's end, at the opposite side, sits the display, a flat rectangular glass window, cold. Your tasks in order. One: explore by touch, find the round dome and the flat window, and check that they sit at opposite ends above the wire row exactly as I said, dome over the white end, window over the red end, and notice whether the dome feels warm. Two: if the layout matches my description, sign thumbs-up. If you cannot find them, or they do not sit as described, sign thumbs-down, and nothing else happens, we regroup. Three: after your thumbs-up, hover your left hand's fingertip over the wire at the end under the cold window, that is the red wire, and hover your right hand's fingertip over the wire at the end under the dome, that is the white wire. Hover above them, skin not touching metal. When both hands hover, sign the two-finger sign. Next round, if all checks hold, you hear the word cut from me, and then in one motion you cut the wire under your left hand, the red one, and immediately, with no pause, the wire under your right hand, the white one. Two cuts, that order, then hands off everything. Memorize it now. Until the word cut, no wire is touched, pressed, or pulled.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍","👏","👋","👏","✍","👏","✊"])
```

TURN 14
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👏 👍 👏 ✍ ✊ 🖐 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]

Decoding round fourteen — and this is the endgame check. Mute: [👍👏👍👏 ✍✊🖐☝] — first thumbs-up confirms my reading of their last message, second thumbs-up answers the manual question exactly as I framed it: *the manual holds nothing else*. Then the dark rule restated one final time in strict format: manual, dark, five, one. So the complete rulebook is now triple-confirmed: red light → cut red. Blue light → cut white. Dark → cut red, then white, immediately, then nothing. No timer clause, no display clause, no third rule. Blind: [👍✌] — layout confirmed: dome found, warm, sitting over the white end; window found, cold, over the red end; both matching my visual description on two independent landmarks. And ✌: both hands hovering — left fingertip over red, right over white. Run the full safety chain: light dark nine straight rounds, so the dark sequence is the live rule. Display zero throughout — and the manual says nothing about the display, so it is not a factor. Blind's map verified empirically, not by assumption — warmth and coldness are things nobody can fake by accident, and they landed exactly where my eyes say they should. My view says red at one end, white at the other; Blind's hands say the same. Mute's manual says the same rule three times over. Every channel agrees, every precondition I set is met, and every round we wait is a round the light could change the rule under us. There is nothing left to learn. I'm giving the order: cut. Red under the left hand first, white under the right in the same motion, then hands off. I report the board next round.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf. All checks hold. Your layout confirmation and hover sign arrived, and the manual is complete: the dark sequence is the live rule, cut the red wire first, then immediately the white wire. Your map was confirmed by two independent landmarks, the warm dome and the cold window, so the translation from my view to your hands is certain. Now the order. The word is: cut. Cut the wire under your left hand, the red one, the one under the cold window. Then in the same motion, with no pause, cut the wire under your right hand, the white one, the one under the warm dome. Two cuts, that order, then take your hands off everything and keep them off. When both cuts are done, sign thumbs-up. Nothing else exists, nothing else follows. Go.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. Your signs read: reading confirmed, manual holds nothing beyond the two rules and the dark sequence, dark means five then one, nothing more. Blind's tactile map matched my view on two independent landmarks, warm dome over the white end, cold window over the red end, and both hands now hover on the correct wires. Light dark nine rounds, display zero throughout. I am giving the cut order this round: red, then immediately white, per the manual. Next round I read the board and report the result to you both.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍","✊","🤝","🖐","🤝","☝"])
```
